peers.name: pdf
peers.description: Use this skill whenever the user wants to do anything with PDF files. This includes reading or extracting text/tables from PDFs, combining or merging multiple PDFs into one, splitting PDFs apart, rotating pages, adding watermarks, creating new PDFs, filling PDF forms, encrypting/decrypting PDFs, extracting images, and OCR on scanned PDFs to make them searchable. If the user mentions a .pdf file or asks to produce one, use this skill.

peers.name: frontend-design
peers.description: Guidance for distinctive, intentional visual design when building new UI or reshaping an existing one. Helps with aesthetic direction, typography, and making choices that don't read as templated defaults.

peers.name: pptx
peers.description: Use this skill any time a .pptx or .potx file is involved in any way — as input, output, or both. This includes: creating slide decks, pitch decks, or presentations; reading, parsing, or extracting text from any .pptx or .potx file (even if the extracted content will be used elsewhere, like in an email or summary); editing, modifying, or updating existing presentations; combining or splitting slide files; working with templates (.potx), layouts, speaker notes, or comments. Trigger whenever the user mentions \"deck,\" \"slides,\" \"presentation,\" or references a .pptx or .potx filename, regardless of what they plan to do with the content afterward. If a .pptx or .potx file needs to be opened, created, or touched, use this skill.

peers.name: docx
peers.description: Use this skill whenever the user wants to create, read, edit, or manipulate Word documents (.docx files) or Word templates (.dotx files). Triggers include: any mention of 'Word doc', 'word document', '.docx', '.dotx', or requests to produce professional documents with formatting like tables of contents, headings, page numbers, or letterheads. Also use when extracting or reorganizing content from .docx or .dotx files, inserting or replacing images in documents, performing find-and-replace in Word files, working with tracked changes or comments, or converting content into a polished Word document. If the user asks for a 'report', 'memo', 'letter', 'template', or similar deliverable as a Word or .docx file, use this skill. Do NOT use for PDFs, spreadsheets, Google Docs, or general coding tasks unrelated to document generation.

en.tagline: Create, test and improve agent skills
en.summary: Skill Creator helps you build a new agent skill or improve an existing one. It covers the whole cycle: defining the skill, writing a draft SKILL.md, running test prompts, reviewing results, and revising. It also includes a method for tuning the skill description so the skill triggers for the right requests.
problem: Writing a skill is easy to start but hard to check. Without test runs, you find out whether a skill works only by trying it by hand. Small changes are hard to compare.

With this skill, test prompts are saved and each one is run with the skill and with a baseline. The outputs are graded against assertions, and a review viewer shows the results. Your feedback then guides the next revision.
fit: Creating a new skill from a workflow in the current conversation
Improving an existing SKILL.md and checking the change against test runs
Tuning a skill description so it triggers for the right requests
unfit: A one-time task that will not be reused as a skill
Comparing two skill versions blind, if your setup cannot run subagents
steps: Capture what the skill should do, when it should trigger, and the expected output format, using the current conversation if it already holds the workflow.
Write a draft SKILL.md with a name and a description that says what the skill does and when to use it.
Save two or three realistic test prompts to `evals/evals.json`, then draft assertions while the runs are in progress.
Run each prompt with the skill and with a baseline in the same turn, then save the results by iteration in a `<skill-name>-workspace/` folder.
Grade the runs, aggregate them with `scripts.aggregate_benchmark`, and open the results with `eval-viewer/generate_review.py` for user review.
Revise the skill based on the feedback, rerun the tests as a new iteration, and optionally optimize the description for triggering accuracy.

zh.tagline: 创建、测试并改进智能体技能
zh.summary: Skill Creator 帮你新建一个智能体技能，或改进已有的技能。它覆盖完整流程：明确技能要做什么，写出 SKILL.md 草稿，运行测试提示词，查看结果，再进行修改。它还提供调整技能描述的方法，让技能在正确的请求下被触发。
problem: 写技能容易开头，难在验证。没有测试运行，只能手动试用来判断技能是否有效，小改动也很难对比。
使用这个技能后，测试提示词会被保存，每条都会分别用技能和基线各运行一次。输出会根据断言打分，并通过审阅查看器展示。你的反馈再用来指导下一版修改。
fit: 把当前对话中的工作流程整理成新技能
改进已有的 SKILL.md，并用测试运行检查改动效果
调整技能描述，使其在正确的请求下被触发
unfit: 只做一次、不会复用为技能的任务
若环境无法运行子代理，就无法进行盲测比较两个技能版本
steps: 明确技能要做什么、何时触发、预期的输出格式；如果当前对话里已有完整流程，就直接从对话中提取。
写出 SKILL.md 草稿，包括名称，以及说明技能用途和使用场景的描述。
在 `evals/evals.json` 中保存两到三条真实的测试提示词，并在测试运行期间起草断言。
每条提示词在同一轮中分别用技能和基线运行，结果按迭代保存在 `<skill-name>-workspace/` 文件夹中。
给运行结果打分，用 `scripts.aggregate_benchmark` 汇总，并用 `eval-viewer/generate_review.py` 打开结果供用户审阅。
根据反馈修改技能，把测试作为新一轮迭代重新运行；也可以选择优化描述，提高触发的准确性。
